attempts.label: CRCNS:vta-1
attempts.entry_title: Medial prefrontal cortex and dopamine reward prediction errors (Starkweather et al. 2018)
attempts.summary: The paper's main findings on VTA dopamine neurons held up in this data. Under saline, reward responses fell with longer delays when reward was certain (task 1) and rose when it was sometimes omitted (task 2), and mPFC inactivation flattened the task 2 rise while leaving task 1 unchanged. The belief state model results reproduced in a Python port of the authors' code, though impaired timing weakens omission responses without abolishing them. The task 2 shift in single-neuron slopes holds only if baseline is subtracted trial by trial, which the paper does not specify. The mPFC recordings (Figure 2) and licking (Figure 3G) could not be tested, as the dataset holds only the 172 identified dopamine neurons.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Starkweather, Gershman and Uchida (2018) on CRCNS vta-1, which holds the spike times of 172 light-identified VTA dopamine neurons, with odor and reward times and trial types, in two classical conditioning tasks after saline or SalB injection. It tests the temporal modulation of post- and pre-reward responses, the slopes of single neurons, the odor B and C and omission responses, and the paper's belief state TD model, ported to Python. Licks, free water deliveries and the mPFC recordings are not in the data set.

As a deviation that decides no outcome, the four tr terms were run without the free water term. On one mean per neuron and ISI none is significant (tr x task 1 p = 0.41, tr x task 2 0.94, tr x drug x task 1 0.99, tr x drug x task 2 0.87); on single trials all four are (p 1.3e-10, 0.021, 0.032 and 0.0086), including tr x drug x task 1, which the paper finds not significant (0.62). Neither is the paper's test, so the claim stays blocked.

outcomes.statement: In task 2, 29 of 41 neurons (70%) had positive slopes of post-reward response on ISI under saline and 12 of 41 negative, while under SalB 24 of 47 (51%) had negative slopes.
outcomes.source: Results, Individual Neurons Recorded in Task 2, paragraph 1; Figure 5F
outcomes.quote: Under the control condition, 29 of 41 neurons (70%) displayed positive slopes (slope [m] > 0), whereas 12 of 41 (29%) displayed negative slopes (Figure 5F). In contrast, 24 of 47 (51%) displayed negative slopes under the inactivation condition
outcomes.notes: With trial-by-trial baseline subtraction, 29 of 41 saline slopes positive and 12 negative, 24 of 47 SalB slopes negative, the paper's counts exactly. With the neuron's mean baseline or none, 28, 13 and 25, also within tolerance. All 172 fits ran, on 83 to 156 trials each.

outcomes.statement: In task 1 the proportion of significant negative against positive slopes did not differ between saline (16 negative, 0 positive) and SalB (16 negative, 2 positive).
outcomes.source: Results, Individual Neurons Recorded in Task 2, paragraph 1; Figure 5E
outcomes.quote: the proportion of significant slopes showing negative versus positive modulation was not significantly different between drug and control conditions (Figure 5E; saline, 16 negative, 0 positive; SalB, 16 negative, 2 positive; p = 0.49, Fisher's exact test)
outcomes.notes: Trial-by-trial baseline, significant slopes saline 16 negative 0 positive, SalB 16 negative 2 positive, Fisher two-sided p = 0.487 (paper 0.49). With the neuron's mean baseline or none, saline 16 and 1, SalB 18 and 2, p = 1; the SalB negative count of 18 is outside the tolerance of 1.6, so the count part holds only under trial-by-trial subtraction, while the absence part holds under every reading. Counting each doubly deposited unit once, SalB 16 and 1, p = 1. Asked of the paper's authors (findings) whether baseline is subtracted trial by trial.
deviations: Assumed that baseline is subtracted trial by trial. The paper says only that "both pre- and post-reward responses were baseline-subtracted, with baseline taken 0-1 s prior to odor onset" (Methods, Data analysis), and the claims file names three readings. Trial by trial is adopted because it is the reading under which the paper's own slope counts are recovered exactly (29, 12 and 24 in task 2; 16, 0, 16 and 2 here) and Fisher p matches the paper's to two digits.

outcomes.statement: In task 2 the proportions of significant negative and positive slopes changed under SalB (saline 1 negative, 9 positive; SalB 9 negative, 7 positive), so neurons were more likely to show significant negative modulation under SalB.
outcomes.source: Results, Individual Neurons Recorded in Task 2, paragraph 1; Figure 5F
outcomes.quote: whereas in task 2, the proportions of significant slopes showing negative versus positive modulation were significantly altered (Figure 5F; saline, 1 negative, 9 positive; SalB, 9 negative, 7 positive; p = 4.1 3 10
outcomes.notes: Trial-by-trial baseline, saline 1 negative 9 positive, SalB 8 negative 7 positive (paper 9 and 7; all within one neuron); the negative share rises from 0.10 to 0.53 and Fisher two-sided p = 0.0405, the paper's 0.041, while the paper's printed counts give 0.0367. With the neuron's mean baseline or none, saline has 3 significant negative slopes and p = 0.239, so the claim does not hold under those readings, and the outcome rests on the trial-by-trial reading. The Methods' wording fits either reading. Trial by trial is the only reading that recovers the printed counts 29, 12 and 24 (task 2 signs) and 16, 0, 16 and 2 (task 1), and both Fisher p values, though here it gives 8 significant negative SalB slopes where the paper prints 9. Keeping the untyped trials or counting the doubly deposited units once gives the same counts and p. Asked of the paper's authors (findings).
deviations: Assumed trial-by-trial baseline subtraction, for the reasons given under fig5e-task1-significant-slopes-unchanged. The outcome depends on it.

outcomes.statement: The belief state TD model reproduces the data with an intact belief state; post-reward RPEs decrease with ISI in task 1 and increase in task 2, most task 2 simulations have positive slopes, pre-reward RPEs decrease in both tasks, and odors B and C give omission responses at the expected reward time.

outcomes.quote: Post-reward firing in task 1 decreased over time (Figure 7C, left) ... Post-reward firing in task 2 increased over time (Figure 7C, right) ... This revealed that the majority of simulations produced positive temporal modulation over time (Figure 7D)
outcomes.notes: 50 simulations; averaged post-reward slope -0.114 (task 1) and +0.149 (task 2) RPE per s; 50 of 50 task 2 simulations positive; pre-reward slopes -0.030 and -0.094; omission responses of B and C -0.181 and -0.131 over the 1 s from the usual reward time. Every part holds in 5 of 5 further seeds and in the code's 10-simulation variant.
deviations: The paper's MATLAB code is run as a line-by-line Python port (belief_td.py), as MATLAB cannot be installed in the entry's locked environment; MATLAB's random streams are replaced by numpy's. No MATLAB or Octave run was available to compare traces with. The author compared blur_matrix, blur_vector, matrices, observations and the tonic, phasic and omission indexing of simulate line by line with blur_matrices_inputWeberFraction.m, blur_vector.m, the four SimulateOdor*.m files and Organize_for_Plotting.m, and found no difference.
"Around the expected reward time" is taken as the 5 sub-states (1 s) from it, the span of the data's omission window (Methods, Data analysis); the minimum near that time is also printed.

outcomes.statement: Impairing hidden state inference in 60% of simulations recapitulates the inactivation data; task 1 post-reward RPEs still decrease, task 2 averaged RPEs flatten, more task 2 simulations have negative slopes than in the intact model, pre-reward RPEs still decrease, and omission responses remain.
outcomes.source: Results, Computational Modeling Implicates the mPFC, paragraph 4; Figure 7F to 7H
outcomes.quote: We could recapitulate our mPFC inactivation data by running 60% of the simulations with this impoverished belief state
outcomes.notes: 30 of 50 task 2 simulations impaired; task 1 slope -0.154; task 2 averaged slope +0.037 against +0.149 intact; negative task 2 slopes 0.32 of simulations against 0.00 intact; task 2 pre-reward slope -0.062; omission responses -0.166 and -0.115. Every part holds in 5 of 5 further seeds.
deviations: The model is the Python port; see fig7cd-model-intact.

outcomes.statement: Impairing timing by blurring the transition matrix flattens task 1 post-reward RPEs and pre-reward RPEs in both tasks, leaves most task 2 simulations with positive slopes, and abolishes omission responses, unlike the data.
outcomes.source: Results, Computational Modeling Implicates the mPFC, paragraph 5; Figure 7I to 7K
outcomes.quote: For example, task 1 post-reward responses were also flattened (Figure 7I, left), pre-reward responses in both tasks 1 and 2 were flattened (Figure 7I, black lines), most simulations still showed positive modulation of post-reward responses over time (Figure 7J), and reward omission responses were abolished (Figure 7K)
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), Weber fraction 0.5 to 1.5 per simulation; task 1 post-reward slope +0.011 against -0.114 intact; pre-reward slopes +0.005 and +0.040 against -0.030 and -0.094; 50 of 50 task 2 slopes positive; omission minima -0.110 and -0.090 against -0.313 and -0.186 intact. Reading (b), 0.56, also meets every part, with a task 1 slope of -0.015 and 49 of 50 task 2 slopes positive, and every part holds in 5 of 5 further seeds under each reading. The dips are reduced, not removed. Over the 50 simulations the mean omission RPE in the 1 s from the usual reward time is -0.073 (SE 0.014, t(49) = -5.05, p = 6.6e-06) for odor B and -0.032 (SE 0.016, p = 0.045) for odor C, 40% and 25% of the intact dips (-0.181 and -0.131); reading (b) gives -0.077 (p = 0.00015) and -0.043 (p = 0.019). The statement's "abolishes" therefore holds only in the weaker sense the criterion tests. Whether the criterion reads the paper rightly is asked of a reader (questions/starkweather-2018.yaml); the outcome is given on the criterion as written.
deviations: The model is the Python port; see fig7cd-model-intact.

findings.statement: The licks, recorded with an infrared beam (Methods), are not in vta-1; the three claims on behavior (Figure 3G, Figure S3) cannot be tested.

Free water deliveries, and so the free water responses that normalize the responses of Figures S5B and S5C and enter two ANOVAs, are not in vta-1; every reward onset in the files belongs to an odor A to C trial.

The mPFC recordings (Figure 2, Figures S1 and S6A to S6E), the unidentified VTA neurons clustered in Figure S4, and the 26 neurons of the no-KORD SalB controls (Figure S6F to S6H) are not in vta-1, which holds only the 172 identified dopamine neurons of the four KORD groups. data.zip has 173 members, the 172 neuron files and the directory entry data/.

No file names its mouse or recording session. Sessions can be recovered as files with identical odor onset arrays (77 sessions), but mice cannot, so the per-mouse analysis of the Figure 5 inset cannot be repeated and results cannot be broken down by animal.

Three pairs of task 1 SalB files share most of their spikes within 0.5 ms (SalB_Task1_9 and SalB_Task1_10, 99.7% of the spikes of the first; SalB_Task1_17 and SalB_Task1_18, 90%; SalB_Task1_36 and SalB_Task1_39, 81%), against at most 1.5% at chance. Each pair is very likely one neuron sorted twice, so task 1 SalB holds 39 distinct neurons, not 42. The paper's statistics include all 42; counting each once changes no outcome.

21 file trials (9 session trials in 8 sessions) are rewarded but have a missing (NaN) trial_type, at delays off the 0.2 s grid (1471 to 2421 ms). The data description does not mention them. They are 5, 1, 1 and 14 neuron trials in task 1 saline, task 1 SalB, task 2 saline and task 2 SalB; kept as odor A trials at the nearest grid ISI, they change no result.

The files give no recording onset or injection time, so the paper's window of the 40 minutes following recording onset cannot be applied exactly. The trials of each session span 23.8 to 38.3 min, consistent with files already cut to that window.

verifications.reviewed: The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper modules vta.py and belief_td.py and the claims file, with the paper's full text. The verifier read the archive's S3 listing, tested _count, auroc, isi_anova and slopes on synthetic inputs, and compared belief_td.py with the MATLAB code at d667730. It had no attempt record. The synthetic checks all came out as expected (_count has a half-open window and gives NaN for a NaN start; auroc gives 1.0 and 0.5 on separable and identical inputs; isi_anova recovers a slope of -2.00 with df (8, 32) for 5 neurons; slopes recovers about -2 under every baseline reading).

paper_notes.statement: The Figure 4A legend gives a pre-reward window of 0 to 200 ms and F(8, 328) = 15 with p = 3.5e-11 for task 1 saline; the Methods give 0 to 400 ms, and the data give F = 9.00, p = 3.6e-11 with the 400 ms window, as the Results print (F > 9.0). The legend's F does not fit its p.
Figure 5F prints 9 significant negative slopes in task 2 under SalB, with Fisher p = 0.041; those counts give p = 0.037. The data give 8, and p = 0.0405.

Question for the paper's authors. For the slopes of single neurons (Figure 5), is the baseline (0 to 1 s before odor onset) subtracted trial by trial, or as the neuron's mean? The two readings give slightly different slopes and p-values. Trial by trial reproduces every printed count and the Fisher p-values; the neuron's mean gives 3 significant negative task 2 saline slopes (paper 1) and a non-significant Fisher test (p = 0.24). This attempt assumes trial by trial.

entries.name: starkweather-2018
entries.title: Medial prefrontal cortex and dopamine reward prediction errors (Starkweather et al. 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Starkweather, Gershman and Uchida (2018) on CRCNS vta-1, which holds the spike times of 172 light-identified VTA dopamine neurons, with odor and reward times and trial types, in two classical conditioning tasks after saline or SalB injection. It tests the temporal modulation of post- and pre-reward responses, the slopes of single neurons, the odor B and C and omission responses, and the paper's belief state TD model, ported to Python. Licks, free water deliveries and the mPFC recordings are not in the data set.
